answer.literal: The library-literal predicate downloads package content and searches decoded string-literal uses in the implementation libraries selected by the exact --tfm net8.0 gesture. Its operand is matched as an ordinal substring of each decoded literal. Preserve case, whitespace, newlines, and all other operand text; there is no normalization. Exactly one distinct operand is allowed: identical repetitions collapse, while distinct operands conflict. A literal needs 1 through 1024 UTF-16 code units. Six hundred astral Unicode characters occupy 1200 UTF-16 code units and are rejected. The empty listed values array is not an allow list and does not mean unrestricted input; the stated constraints govern acceptance. --tfm and library-literal require each other, and the target goes through --tfm rather than --where.
answer.dependency: The preferred exact predicate is depends=Newtonsoft.Json with dependency-depth=3 and dependency-target=net8.0. With depth, exact depends matches direct paths and transitive declaration paths through the maximum of three edges. Without depth, exact depends matches direct dependencies; starts-with also remains direct and cannot alone admit depth. Legacy depends-transitive=Newtonsoft.Json with the same target and depth matches only paths of depth 2 through 3, so it excludes direct-only hits. Allowed depth values are 2, 3, and 4. Depth 1 is invalid. A depth query requires an exact depends term or legacy depends-transitive and an explicit framework target; dependency-target=all is invalid for this command. Repeated exact terms are ANDed and share traversal. Dependency target scopes dependency predicates to the selected manifest group. No additional normalization of package IDs or target frameworks is asserted by the inspected resources.
answer.candidate_vs_rows: For a Microsoft.Azure.* prefix population, use positional Microsoft.Azure.* with --take 5 to cap package candidates admitted for inspection and -n 2 to return at most two final rows, plus the desired --where terms and --json. A smaller --take such as 2 also satisfies the candidate cap but may miss later qualifying packages. -n 2 alone does not bound candidate work. These inspection predicates admit at most five candidates; an exact package ID admits one.
